item.title: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics has gone to a neutrino detector in Antarctica
item.description: The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin Madison, who built an observatory under Antarctica.
item.content:encoded: The Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded Francis Halzen of the University of Wisconsin Madison, who built an observatory under Antarctica.

item.title: Germany's ex-foreign intelligence agency chief is arrested on suspicion of espionage
item.description: Germany's former foreign intelligence agency chief has been arrested on suspicion of treasonous espionage. A former high-ranking aide has also been arrested.
item.content:encoded: Germany's former foreign intelligence agency chief has been arrested on suspicion of treasonous espionage. A former high-ranking aide has also been arrested.

item.title: France protests continue
item.description: French high school students are marched together as they demanded better learning conditions at their schools. Several hundred thousand students turned out in cities across France.
item.content:encoded: French high school students are marched together as they demanded better learning conditions at their schools. Several hundred thousand students turned out in cities across France.

item.title: 'Medicare for All' message attracts midterm voters buckling under medical bills
item.description: Midterm candidates are talking about Medicare for All, and two out of three Americans tell pollsters they support it. It speaks to the desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.

item.description: Five years after the U.S.'s withdrawal from Afghanistan, the Taliban remains firmly in power. Here's how the Taliban doing in terms of foreign policy.

item.description: British police said they had made a seventh arrest in a murky plot that may have targeted a U.K. airbase.

item.title: CDC funding for HIV prevention shifted from providers to states under Trump
item.description: Nonprofits fighting HIV used get direct funding from the CDC. Now that money is going to state health departments that may have other priorities.

item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with marine ecologist Jeff Seminoff about the first known natural sea turtle nesting on California's shores.

item.title: Cubans in U.S. sour on Trump's immigration policies
item.description: Cubans in the U.S. are growing frustrated with President Trump's immigration policies, which has resulted in their detention and the dismissal of protections that have benefitted Cubans specifically.
